title: Verification harness: tiers, headless launches, fewer samples and concurrency
objective: Cut the wall-clock and agent cost of rendered and timing evidence without weakening any oracle: one aggregate command with tiers and a summary, hidden-window launches with a focus check, defaults sized to what each statistic needs, and safe concurrency for rendered runs.
context_summary: The evidence harness launches the editor per sample: raw-editor defaults to 30 samples with two launches each per source, measure to 30 per workload, and every smoke scenario is a separate launch and a separate agent tool call whose frames get read as images. Runs are serial, and the LSBackgroundOnly bundle stops activation but still shows a window. Timing figures were repeatedly noisy from concurrent load. The exactness oracles (small fixtures, hand-counted histograms, f64 references) are cheap and stay.

tasks.description: Lower the launch multipliers: raw-editor defaults to 3 samples, measure to 5, and the docs state that p95 claims need the timing tier.
extra_context: raw-editor launches the editor twice per sample per source, so its 30-sample default is about 180 launches for a three-source manifest; one sample proves the journey.
editor-latency already takes its 30 samples inside one launch and keeps its default.

Read the docs diff for every mention of the defaults.
expected_results: Default runs launch the editor 6 times per source for raw-editor and 5 per workload for measure; the docs match.

tasks.description: Add cargo xtask verify with quick, rendered, timing and full tiers that runs the selected commands and writes one summary.
extra_context: quick = check plus editor-acceptance; rendered adds every smoke scenario; timing adds editor-performance, editor-latency and measure; full adds raw-editor and raw-reference when a manifest is given.

The summary is one summary.json plus a short Markdown table: pass or fail per scenario, p50/p95 per timing row, each provisional target with its measured figure and verdict, and the artifact path of every run. Stdout prints only the table.
Frames are not opened by the command; an agent reads images only for a failed scenario or a design review.

acceptance_criteria: One command runs a tier end to end into a fresh output directory and exits non-zero if any component fails, naming it.
summary.json and summary.md hold every component's status, timing rows, target verdicts and artifact paths, and the console shows only the table.
A partial failure still writes the summary for the components that ran.
The docs describe the tiers and say the local default is quick, with rendered and timing run at integration points.

steps: Run quick and rendered tiers on the M4 and inspect the summaries.
Force a scenario failure and confirm the exit code and the summary entry.
expected_results: Each tier produces one summary an agent can read without opening artifacts.

tasks.description: Add a hidden-window evidence mode and make it the default for every automated launch, with a launcher check that no focus change occurred.
extra_context: The LSBackgroundOnly bundle prevents activation, but the evidence window is still created visible; nothing needs it on screen.

First verify on the M4 that renderer readbacks, the render_ready correlation and GPU upload timing still work with iced window visible = false; if they do not, report the finding and keep the window visible with a documented reason rather than faking captures.
The launcher records the frontmost application before and after each launch (for example through osascript) and fails the run when it changed.

acceptance_criteria: An evidence flag creates the window hidden; smoke, measure, editor-latency and raw-editor pass it by default and develop does not.
Every smoke scenario, measure and editor-latency pass with the hidden window on the M4 and their frames are unchanged in content.
The launcher's focus check is recorded in each result JSON and fails the run on a change.
If hidden rendering cannot capture frames, the reason is recorded in the docs and the flag stays off for smoke only.

steps: Run every smoke scenario and the timing commands with the hidden window; compare frame checks with a visible run.
Watch the desktop during a run and read the recorded focus check.
expected_results: No window appears during automated runs and every scenario still passes with identical checks.

tasks.description: Run rendered scenarios concurrently in the verify command and serialize timing runs behind a load gate.
extra_context: Scenarios use isolated catalogs and output directories; they share the GPU, so bound the pool (three or four at once) and measure whether wall-clock drops without failures.

Timing tiers stay serial, refuse to start while another xtask timing run is alive, and record the one-minute load average; figures above a stated load are marked unreliable in the summary rather than recorded as baselines.

acceptance_criteria: The rendered tier runs scenarios in a bounded pool and its summary shows per-scenario and total wall-clock against the serial time.
Timing tiers are serial, the load gate and its threshold are recorded in every timing summary, and a busy host marks figures unreliable.
No scenario shares a catalog, evidence directory or port with another.

steps: Run the rendered tier serially and concurrently and compare results and wall-clock.
Start two timing runs and confirm the second refuses.
expected_results: Concurrent rendered runs pass with the same checks in less wall-clock; timing runs never overlap.

tasks.description: Point CI and the working rules at the tiers, and decide from measured run times which rendered scenarios belong in the rendered tier versus full.
extra_context: CI keeps its headless Xvfb scenarios; local guidance becomes: quick per change, rendered and timing at integration points, full before a milestone claim.
Retire no oracle: the small fixtures and hand-counted histograms are the exactness proofs and cost seconds.
